rationale: In Old English, "hring" (abbreviated G) most commonly denotes a finger-ring or circular band of precious metal, a ubiquitous item in Anglo-Saxon material culture and poetry (e.g., the lord as "hringdrihten," ring-giver). The jewelry sense (ring.n.08) best matches this concrete, literal usage, consistent with the primary meaning of OE hring as an ornamental circlet worn on the finger or given as treasure.
